The '''Minavar system''' was a [[Star system/Legends|star system]]<ref name="Gambler" /> located within the [[Bheriz sector/Legends|Bheriz sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> a part of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of<ref name="Slice" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> At some point, an expedition that included the [[Human/Legends|Human]] infant [[Reina Gale]] and her family established a [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] within the system.<ref name="Gambler" /> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Date">The events of the narrative sections of {{JournalCite|4|It's a Gambler's Life}} are set during the existence of the [[Pentastar Alignment]], no less than twelve [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after [[Reina Gale]] became an orphan. Since ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' states the Alignment was absorbed by the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], it can therefore be deduced that Gale's [[Parent/Legends|parents]] [[Death/Legends|died]] in no later than [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> however, the colony was ravaged by a virus that [[Death/Legends|killed]] nearly its entire population, including Gale's [[Parent/Legends|parents]], and the [[Gender/Legends|girl]] was left in the care of [[Reina Gale's uncle|her uncle]].<ref name="Gambler" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Minavar system was first mentioned in the [[1994]] [[roleplaying game]] article "[[It's a Gambler's Life]]." The article was written by [[Tony Russo|Anthony P. Russo]] and published in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 4|fourth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine.<ref name="Gambler" />

When the [[1998]] ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' gave the system an entry, its name was misspelled as "Mindavar system."<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Minavar system within grid square U-10.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>
